title: Cap. III Rat. 5: foresight election would be acceptor personarum
pass_a_gloss: Reason 5. If God from foreseen merits should elect certain ones to glory, others being passed by, he would be an acceptor of persons. For a just and rational election presupposes a certain disparity between the elect and the non-elect; and the prudent always elects what is better. Since therefore no difference can be thought up between men apart from this foresight of merits in some, which are not foreseen in others, it follows that we should say that God's election always rests on this sort of foresight of human merits.
pass_b_english: Rat. 5. If God elected some to glory from foresight of merits and passed others by, he would be an acceptor of persons. A just, rational election presupposes some disparity between elect and non-elect, and the prudent always chooses what is better. Since no difference among people can be imagined apart from foresight of merits in some that are not foreseen in others, it follows that God's election always rests on that kind of foresight of human merits.
source_text: Rat. 5. Si Deus ex meritis praevisis eligeret quosdam ad gloriam, aliis praeteritis, esset acceptor personarum. Nam electio justa et rationabilis disparitatem quandam inter electos et non-electos praesupponit; et prudens semper quod est melius eligit. Cum ergo nulla excogitari possit differentia inter homines absque hac praevisione meritorum in aliquibus, quae non praevidentur in aliis, consequens est ut dicamus, electionem Dei semper inniti hujusmodi praescientiae humanorum meritorum.
